wb8_demolish.topic: Demolitions, Masafer Yatta, Khan al-Ahmar, Sheikh Jarrah

claims.text: In 2025 Israeli authorities demolished 1,657 Palestinian structures in the West Bank; 1,538 (93%) for lack of Israeli-issued building permits, 87 punitive or other, 32 in military operations. 416 were inhabited homes, 546 agricultural.

OCHA counted 37,135 Palestinians displaced in the West Bank in 2025: about 35,000 by military operations (33,362 from the northern camps), 1,964 by demolitions, 151 by settler violence and access restrictions.

Over 1,000 people displaced by lack-of-permit demolitions in Area C in 2025, second-highest since 2009; nearly 12,000 displaced in Area C 2009–2025, about 65% (7,639) in Bedouin and herding communities. Punitive demolitions since 7 Oct 2023: 420 displaced from 87 structures.

Firing Zone 918 declared in early 1980s (~7,400 acres) over the Masafer Yatta area, home to over 1,000 Palestinians in eight villages; on 4 May 2022 Israel's Supreme Court rejected the residents' petitions, accepting the state's case that they had not proven permanent residence before the zone was declared and treating the ban on forcible transfer as a treaty norm not enforceable in Israeli courts. UN experts and NRC criticized the ruling.

Khan al-Ahmar: fewer than 200 Jahalin Bedouin; Supreme Court approved demolition in 2018; state says structures built without permits and dangerously near a highway; residents say permits are almost never given; relocation site near Abu Dis with utilities and a school; demolition repeatedly postponed by governments amid EU and international pressure; Regavim petitioned to force it.

Sheikh Jarrah: the 1970 Legal and Administrative Matters Law lets Jews reclaim East Jerusalem property lost in 1948, while the 1950 Absentees' Property Law prevents Palestinians reclaiming property in Israel; NRC counted about 970 Palestinians at risk of eviction in East Jerusalem in 2021, 218 households with cases.

March 2022 Supreme Court ruling let four Karem al-Ja'uni families stay at least until land registration completes; April 2024 the Magistrate's Court ordered the Diab family (23 people) evicted in a suit by Nahalat Shimon, which holds the claim of two Jewish associations that bought the land in the late 19th century.
May 2026: Smotrich ordered preparations to evacuate Khan al-Ahmar (about 300 people); the order needed cabinet approval and had not been signed; school of 170+ children.
Diab family: District Court rejected appeal Feb 2025; Supreme Court granted leave to appeal and froze the eviction Nov 2025.

claims.text: Yesh Din, 2005–2025: 93.6% of the police files it monitored on settler violence closed without indictment; about 3% led to full or partial conviction.
OCHA counted 1,828 settler attacks causing casualties or damage in 2025, up from 1,449 in 2024; 2025 deaths: 240 Palestinians killed (225 by forces, 9 by settlers), 17 Israelis killed.
2025 to 8 Dec: 772 Palestinians injured by settlers; attacks in 270+ communities; Ein Samiya fully displaced.

26 Feb 2023: a Palestinian gunman killed brothers Hillel and Yagel Yaniv near Huwara; that night hundreds of settlers set fire to homes, businesses and cars; one Palestinian killed, about 100 injured; army commander Yehuda Fox called it a pogrom; Smotrich said Huwara should be wiped out and later retracted; arrested suspects were released.

OCHA, 1 Nov 2023: since 7 Oct, 15 herding communities, 98 households (828 people) displaced amid settler violence and restrictions; in almost half of incidents involving firearms Israeli forces accompanied or supported attackers; Khirbet Zanuta 24 households displaced 28 Oct.

Kerem Navot data (Dec 2024): 57 communities displaced since Oct 2023 (50 fully, 7 partly); at least 41 outposts and herding farms set up since Oct 2023; Zanuta residents returned under a High Court ruling Aug 2024 and left again; five settlers indicted for the Muarrajat school attack.

Peace Now/Kerem Navot 2025: over 100 shepherding outposts; settlers control at least 786,000 dunams (~14% of the West Bank) through grazing; state funds include NIS 54m security budget, Agriculture Ministry grazing grants (~NIS 3m 2017–24), Settlement Division grants and ~80,000 dunams allocated for grazing.

Nov 2025: Netanyahu said Israel would take forceful action, that extremists are a minority not representing law-abiding settlers; IDF chief Zamir said attacks 'cross a red line'; Herzog called them shocking; police probes of settler violence fell to 60 in 2025 from 235 in 2023 (Channel 12); IDF counted 704 'nationalistic crime' incidents in 2025 to mid-Nov.
